ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Concerns about developmental delays and failure to crawl with observed right-sided preference

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with Holoprosencephaly returns for follow-up one year after ED presentation for poor feeding and intermittent seizures, and is brought to the pediatrician by his parents due to concerns about development. They report that he has not yet started to crawl, and they have noticed that he seems to favor his right side.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Holoprosencephaly (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Holoprosencephaly (lobar type)
- Spastic hemiplegic cerebral palsy
- Epilepsy
- Global developmental delay
- Prematurity (32 weeks gestation)
- Failure to thrive
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease
- Hypotonia with asymmetric spasticity

His birth history is significant for preterm delivery at 32 weeks gestation, and he required a two-week stay in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory support and monitoring.

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Gastrostomy tube placement (Mic-Key button)
- Nissen fundoplication
- Ventricular-peritoneal shunt placement

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Levetiracetam 100 mg (1 mL of 100 mg/mL solution) orally twice daily
- Baclofen 2.5 mg (0.5 mL of 5 mg/5 mL suspension) orally twice daily
- Omeprazole 5 mg (half of 10 mg packet) orally once daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal gestational diabetes mellitus
- Paternal second cousin with cleft lip/palate (midline defect)
- Consanguinity (parents are second cousins)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Pediatric patient (Early Intervention Program).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child has a persistent fisted right hand and seems to drag his right leg when attempting to move. His right arm and leg appear stiffer than the left. Deep tendon reflexes are 3+ in the right biceps, brachioradialis, and patellar tendons. Ankle clonus is present on the right side. The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.
